        data[tid].append((row['timestamp'], float(row['value'])))
for k in data: data[k].sort()

# Check variance (sensor health)
import statistics
for k,name in ids.items():
    vals=[v for _,v in data[k]]
    print(name, 'mean=%.2f'%statistics.mean(vals), 'stdev=%.3f'%statistics.stdev(vals), 'min=%.2f'%min(vals), 'max=%.2f'%max(vals), 'n=%d'%len(vals))

The VAV_F3_Z01 Damper_Position_Setpoint simultaneously rose from ~0.2 to ~0.44 in July 2018 (and back to ~0.23 in Jan 2019), i.e. the controller opened the damper more to cool the zone — the expected response to a genuine local heat-load increase. Under a sensor fault (offset/drift high), the controller would close the damper (or hit its limit), not open it; the damper's matching ramp-up argues against a sensor-only fault.
